tactics.body: Almost always the wrong button for a Paladin, and your app should say so plainly. : (a) your Lay on Hands pool is empty; (b) you need burst healing bigger than the pool can deliver in one Bonus Action; (c) you are out of melee range of anything worth hitting anyway.

detail.subtitle: Bonus action · 1st-level slot

facts.label: Casting Time
facts.value: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

facts.label: Damage
facts.value: 2d8 Radiant (+1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Paladin level 2 (Paladin's Smite) - always prepared; one free cast per Long Rest with no slot

detail.whatItDoes: Immediately after you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you spend your Bonus Action to channel 2d8 extra Radiant damage into that hit, plus another 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

ruleBox.text: Casting this spends your 1st slot AND your one levelled spell slot for the turn. Nothing else levelled can follow it this turn.

tactics.lead: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN YOUR ENTIRE KIT, AND THE ONE APPS GET WRONG
tactics.body: : 2024 says 'On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.' You cannot cast Bless and then Divine Smite in the same turn. You cannot Smite twice in a turn. One slot, one turn, no exceptions.

tactics.lead: THE LOOPHOLE THAT IS ACTUALLY LEGAL
tactics.body: : your level 2 Paladin's Smite feature lets you cast Divine Smite once per Long Rest WITHOUT EXPENDING A SLOT. The one-slot rule restricts EXPENDING slots. So on one turn per long rest you can legally cast a slotted spell with your Action and free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. Save that turn for the round you need to open hardest.

tactics.lead: SMITE AFTER YOU SEE THE ROLL
tactics.body: : you cast this AFTER the hit is confirmed, not before. Never pre-commit. Attack, see the number, then decide. This is the single biggest reason Divine Smite beats Searing Smite on efficiency — no wasted slots on misses.

tactics.lead: CRITICAL HITS DOUBLE THE SMITE DICE
tactics.body: : on a crit you roll all the attack's damage dice twice, and the Smite dice are part of that attack's damage. A crit with a level 2 slot is 6d8 of Smite. So SMITE ON CRITS, ALWAYS, without hesitation, even against a target you would not otherwise spend a slot on.

: with Extra Attack you get two swings. Take the first swing. If it crits, Smite immediately. If it hits normally, hold — take the second swing, and if THAT crits, Smite it instead. You only get one Smite per turn either way, so let the dice tell you which hit deserves it.

: Fiends and Undead take +1d8. Concentrating enemy casters are the real prize — a big Smite forces a Concentration save at DC 10 or half the damage, and a 2nd-level Smite averaging 13 means a DC 10 save, while a crit for 27 means a DC 13. Dropping an enemy's Wall of Force or Hold Person is worth more than the raw damage.
: the casting time explicitly names Unarmed Strikes. If you are grappling something and cannot draw a weapon, you can still Smite it.

: no bows, no crossbows. Thrown melee weapons (javelin, handaxe) are a genuine RAW dispute — make this a configurable toggle in your app and ask your DM which way it rules. detail.whatItDoes: You bear the manifestation of the Hearthfire both within and without. This manifestation appears in a form you choose, such as a small floating ember, a dancing flame, or a spirit. The manifestation sheds Bright Light for 10 feet and Dim Light for 10 additional feet. If this manifestation goes beyond 30 feet from you, it is extinguished. It can be summoned or dismissed as a Bonus Action. As a Reaction, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and issue a command word, causing the Essence of the Hearth to transform into a flaming cloak. The cloak immediately grants you Temporary Hit Points equal to your Paladin level plus your spellcasting ability modifier. When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage in retaliation. This effect lasts until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted.

errata.problem: The cloak is activated 'As a Reaction' but no trigger is defined. 2024 requires every Reaction to state its trigger: 'A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description.' Without a trigger the feature cannot be legally used.
errata.note: No official Paladin Channel Divinity option uses a Reaction; they use a Bonus Action or the Magic action. This is a genuine departure.
errata.recommendedFix: Define the trigger explicitly. Suggested: 'As a Reaction, which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity...' Alternatively convert to a Bonus Action to match official Channel Divinity options.
errata.appAction: Require the player to record a chosen trigger with DM approval, then enforce it. Default suggestion: 'when you take damage'.

errata.problem: The cloak lasts 'until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted'. In 2024 Temporary Hit Points DO NOT STACK - when you gain new Temporary Hit Points you choose to keep the old pool or take the new one. Taking any other source of Temporary Hit Points (Heroism, Inspiring Leader, Orc Adrenaline Rush, a Chef treat, Aid does not apply) REPLACES the cloak's pool, which by the feature's own wording ends the cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Add: 'The cloak lasts for 1 minute, or until the Temporary Hit Points granted by this feature are reduced to 0, whichever comes first. Gaining Temporary Hit Points from another source does not end this effect.' This decouples the duration from the temp HP pool.
errata.appAction: MANDATORY WARNING. If the cloak is active and the player gains Temporary Hit Points from another source, the app must prompt: 'Accepting these Temporary Hit Points will replace your Hearthfire cloak pool and end the cloak. Continue?'

errata.problem: The retaliation clause has no limit on frequency. 'When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage' triggers on every melee hit, with no once-per-turn or once-per-round cap and no Reaction cost.
errata.comparison: The Fire Shield spell (level 4) deals 2d8 on the same trigger with the same lack of cap, so unlimited retaliation is not unprecedented. However, Fire Shield is a level 4 spell with a hard 10-minute duration; the cloak is a level 3 Channel Divinity whose duration is tied to a temp HP pool that can be large.
errata.assessment: Acceptable as written at low levels. At level 20 with a large temp HP pool this could run for a very long time.
errata.recommendedFix: Optional: cap the duration at 1 minute (see HEARTH-04), which naturally bounds it.
errata.appAction: Implement as written but display the total retaliation damage dealt per encounter so the DM can see the real numbers.

errata.problem: Unclear whether the manifestation must be summoned before the cloak can be used, and whether summoning it costs a separate Bonus Action from the Reaction that activates the cloak. Also undefined: how the manifestation moves, whether it occupies a space, whether it can be attacked or targeted, and whether it provides light while worn as a cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Rule that the manifestation must be active to transform into the cloak; that it moves with you automatically (treat it as an effect on your person, not a creature or object); that it cannot be attacked or damaged; and that the cloak sheds the same light as the manifestation.
errata.appAction: Record these as a house-ruling block the player fills in once with DM approval.

detail.title: Sacred Flame
detail.subtitle: Action · no slot

facts.label: Damage
facts.value: 1d8 (2d8 at character level 5, 3d8 at 11, 4d8 at 17) Radiant

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability

detail.whatItDoes: Flame-like radiance descends on a creature you can see within range. It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 Radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Cover for this save. The damage increases at character levels 5, 11 and 17.

tactics.body: The standard ranged answer for a Blessed Warrior Paladin, and the choice between this and Toll the Dead is the real decision.

— that is Sacred Flame's unique selling point and it is genuinely valuable. An archer behind a wall, an enemy in a murder hole, a caster peeking around a corner: cover normally gives +2 or +5 to Dexterity saves and AC. Sacred Flame ignores it entirely. Against a fortified position this is the only ranged option in your kit that works. IT USES A SAVE, NOT AN ATTACK ROLL, so a high-AC target does not blunt it — but a high-Dexterity target does. It is the mirror image of Scorching Ray: use Sacred Flame against armored, low-Dexterity enemies and Scorching Ray against agile, low-AC ones.
: rarely resisted, and it is the same type as your Divine Smite and your level 11 Radiant Strikes, which keeps your damage profile consistent.

tactics.lead: SACRED FLAME VS TOLL THE DEAD
tactics.body: : Toll the Dead does more damage (1d12 against a wounded target versus 1d8) and Necrotic is resisted about as rarely as Radiant. Sacred Flame ignores cover; Toll the Dead uses a Wisdom save. Take Sacred Flame if your campaign has fortifications and undead; take Toll the Dead if you want raw numbers. Do not take both — they overlap almost completely and you only get two cantrips.
: at level 5+ with Extra Attack, two weapon swings almost always beat one cantrip. This is your answer for the rounds you CANNOT reach melee, not your default action.

detail.title: Shield of Faith
detail.subtitle: Bonus action · 1st-level slot
detail.whatItDoes: A shimmering field gives one creature within 60 feet a +2 bonus to Armor Class for the duration.

ruleBox.text: Casting this spends your 1st slot AND your one levelled spell slot for the turn. Nothing else levelled can follow it this turn.

tactics.body: Ten minutes of +2 AC for one level 1 slot and a Bonus Action, at 60 feet. That is the best damage-mitigation-per-slot ratio you have.

: at level 7 in Plate (18) with a Shield (+2) and the Defense fighting style (+1) you are at 21. Shield of Faith makes it 23. Against a typical CR 7 attacker with +7 to hit, going from 21 to 23 drops their hit rate from 35%% to 25%% — that is nearly a 30%% cut in incoming damage, sustained for the whole fight.
: ten-minute duration means you can cast it in the corridor, not the doorway. A Paladin who walks into every room already at +2 AC is a different character from one who spends round one buffing.

— THIS IS THE REAL CHOICE OF YOUR CAREER: you can run exactly one of Bless, Shield of Faith, Compelled Duel, or Protection from Evil and Good. The rule of thumb: Bless when the party's offense is the bottleneck, Shield of Faith when YOUR survival is the bottleneck, Compelled Duel when your party's survival is the bottleneck. Bless is usually right in a party of four or more; Shield of Faith is right when you are alone, escorting, or holding a chokepoint. 60-FOOT RANGE IS THE HIDDEN FEATURE: you can put this on a squishy ally across the room without leaving your position. Most Paladins self-cast it on reflex and waste that reach.

detail.title: Warding Bond
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Components
facts.value: V, S, M (a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A willing creature you touch gains +1 AC, +1 to all saving throws, and Resistance to all damage. While the bond lasts, every time that creature takes damage, YOU take the same amount of damage. The bond breaks if either of you drops to 0 HP, or if you move more than 60 feet apart.

ruleBox.text: Casting this spends your 2nd slot AND your one levelled spell slot for the turn. Nothing else levelled can follow it this turn.

tactics.body: This is THE Oath of the Hearth spell, mechanically and thematically. 'Guard the hearth' is literally what it does — you take the wound instead of the person you are protecting.

tactics.lead: HOW THE RESISTANCE MATH ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT IS GOOD
tactics.body: : the target takes HALF damage, and YOU take the amount THEY took after resistance. So a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 10 to you. Total damage to the party is unchanged — but you have MOVED it from a d6-hit-die caster with 30 HP onto a d10 Paladin with heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and a healing pool. That is the entire point: you are not reducing damage, you are relocating it onto the character best equipped to absorb it. COMBINE WITH YOUR AURA OF SOLACE (level 7): you have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic. Warding Bond damage is damage YOU take — if your DM rules it retains its damage type (most do), your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN. Warding Bond a caster against a fire-breathing enemy and a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you. That is the strongest defensive combination in the entire Hearth build and your app should surface it explicitly.

tactics.lead: THE COMPONENT COST YOUR APP MUST TRACK
tactics.body: : 100 GP of platinum rings, and they are WORN, not consumed — so you buy them once and reuse them forever. But you must actually own them, a focus cannot substitute, and the target has to be wearing one. Put them in your equipment list now.

tactics.lead: THE 60-FOOT LEASH IS A TACTICAL CONSTRAINT
tactics.body: : the bond breaks if you separate. That means you cannot bond the scout. Bond the person who will stand near you — usually the same person standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection. Your positioning doctrine and your bonding choice should be the same decision.
: it breaks when YOU hit 0. If you are already hurt, bonding someone can kill you both. Check your own HP before casting. Never bond while below half.
: it runs alongside Bless or Compelled Duel. This is a huge deal — it is the only major defensive buff you own that does not compete for Concentration.

: your oath grants Warding Bond as an always-prepared spell at Paladin level 5, and it is ALSO on the standard Paladin spell list. Do not spend one of your seven prepared-spell picks on it. Your app must dedupe this or you will silently waste a prepared slot.

facts.label: Casting Time

facts.value: 2d8 Radiant (+1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead)

detail.whatItDoes: Immediately after you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you spend your Bonus Action to channel 2d8 extra Radiant damage into that hit, plus another 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.lead: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN YOUR ENTIRE KIT, AND THE ONE APPS GET WRONG
tactics.body: : 2024 says 'On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.' You cannot cast Bless and then Divine Smite in the same turn. You cannot Smite twice in a turn. One slot, one turn, no exceptions.

tactics.lead: THE LOOPHOLE THAT IS ACTUALLY LEGAL
tactics.body: : your level 2 Paladin's Smite feature lets you cast Divine Smite once per Long Rest WITHOUT EXPENDING A SLOT. The one-slot rule restricts EXPENDING slots. So on one turn per long rest you can legally cast a slotted spell with your Action and free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. Save that turn for the round you need to open hardest.

tactics.lead: SMITE AFTER YOU SEE THE ROLL
tactics.body: : you cast this AFTER the hit is confirmed, not before. Never pre-commit. Attack, see the number, then decide. This is the single biggest reason Divine Smite beats Searing Smite on efficiency — no wasted slots on misses.

tactics.lead: CRITICAL HITS DOUBLE THE SMITE DICE
tactics.body: : on a crit you roll all the attack's damage dice twice, and the Smite dice are part of that attack's damage. A crit with a level 2 slot is 6d8 of Smite. So SMITE ON CRITS, ALWAYS, without hesitation, even against a target you would not otherwise spend a slot on.

: with Extra Attack you get two swings. Take the first swing. If it crits, Smite immediately. If it hits normally, hold — take the second swing, and if THAT crits, Smite it instead. You only get one Smite per turn either way, so let the dice tell you which hit deserves it.

: Fiends and Undead take +1d8. Concentrating enemy casters are the real prize — a big Smite forces a Concentration save at DC 10 or half the damage, and a 2nd-level Smite averaging 13 means a DC 10 save, while a crit for 27 means a DC 13. Dropping an enemy's Wall of Force or Hold Person is worth more than the raw damage.
: the casting time explicitly names Unarmed Strikes. If you are grappling something and cannot draw a weapon, you can still Smite it.

: no bows, no crossbows. Thrown melee weapons (javelin, handaxe) are a genuine RAW dispute — make this a configurable toggle in your app and ask your DM which way it rules. HEARTH SYNERGY (level 15): Smoldering Smite adds 1d8 Fire that ignores resistance AND immunity. The manifestation sheds Bright Light for 10 feet and Dim Light for 10 additional feet. If this manifestation goes beyond 30 feet from you, it is extinguished. As a Reaction, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and issue a command word, causing the Essence of the Hearth to transform into a flaming cloak. errata.problem: The cloak is activated 'As a Reaction' but no trigger is defined. 2024 requires every Reaction to state its trigger: 'A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description.' Without a trigger the feature cannot be legally used.
errata.note: No official Paladin Channel Divinity option uses a Reaction; they use a Bonus Action or the Magic action. This is a genuine departure.
errata.recommendedFix: Define the trigger explicitly. Suggested: 'As a Reaction, which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity...' Alternatively convert to a Bonus Action to match official Channel Divinity options.
errata.appAction: Require the player to record a chosen trigger with DM approval, then enforce it. Default suggestion: 'when you take damage'.

errata.problem: The cloak lasts 'until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted'. In 2024 Temporary Hit Points DO NOT STACK - when you gain new Temporary Hit Points you choose to keep the old pool or take the new one. Taking any other source of Temporary Hit Points (Heroism, Inspiring Leader, Orc Adrenaline Rush, a Chef treat, Aid does not apply) REPLACES the cloak's pool, which by the feature's own wording ends the cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Add: 'The cloak lasts for 1 minute, or until the Temporary Hit Points granted by this feature are reduced to 0, whichever comes first. Gaining Temporary Hit Points from another source does not end this effect.' This decouples the duration from the temp HP pool.
errata.appAction: MANDATORY WARNING. If the cloak is active and the player gains Temporary Hit Points from another source, the app must prompt: 'Accepting these Temporary Hit Points will replace your Hearthfire cloak pool and end the cloak. Continue?'

errata.problem: The retaliation clause has no limit on frequency. 'When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage' triggers on every melee hit, with no once-per-turn or once-per-round cap and no Reaction cost.
errata.comparison: The Fire Shield spell (level 4) deals 2d8 on the same trigger with the same lack of cap, so unlimited retaliation is not unprecedented. However, Fire Shield is a level 4 spell with a hard 10-minute duration; the cloak is a level 3 Channel Divinity whose duration is tied to a temp HP pool that can be large.
errata.assessment: Acceptable as written at low levels. At level 20 with a large temp HP pool this could run for a very long time.
errata.recommendedFix: Optional: cap the duration at 1 minute (see HEARTH-04), which naturally bounds it.
errata.appAction: Implement as written but display the total retaliation damage dealt per encounter so the DM can see the real numbers.

errata.problem: Unclear whether the manifestation must be summoned before the cloak can be used, and whether summoning it costs a separate Bonus Action from the Reaction that activates the cloak. Also undefined: how the manifestation moves, whether it occupies a space, whether it can be attacked or targeted, and whether it provides light while worn as a cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Rule that the manifestation must be active to transform into the cloak; that it moves with you automatically (treat it as an effect on your person, not a creature or object); that it cannot be attacked or damaged; and that the cloak sheds the same light as the manifestation.
errata.appAction: Record these as a house-ruling block the player fills in once with DM approval.

detail.title: Burning Hands
detail.subtitle: Action · 1st-level slot

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 3 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A sheet of flame shoots from your outspread fingers in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in the area takes 3d6 Fire damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity save. It also ignites flammable objects in the area that no one is holding or wearing.

tactics.body: Your only crowd-clearing option until level 17's Flame Strike, and at level 7 it is worth more than it looks.

tactics.body: : at level 7 with Extra Attack you swing twice for roughly 20 damage to ONE target. Burning Hands upcast to level 2 is 4d6 (avg 14) to EVERY creature in a 15-foot cone. Against three enemies that is 42 damage for one Action and one level 2 slot. Two or more targets and the spell wins; one target and it loses badly. tactics.lead: THE POSITIONING PROBLEM AND THE FIX

detail.whatItDoes: Immediately after you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you spend your Bonus Action to channel 2d8 extra Radiant damage into that hit, plus another 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

detail.whatItDoes: You bear the manifestation of the Hearthfire both within and without. This manifestation appears in a form you choose, such as a small floating ember, a dancing flame, or a spirit. The manifestation sheds Bright Light for 10 feet and Dim Light for 10 additional feet. If this manifestation goes beyond 30 feet from you, it is extinguished. It can be summoned or dismissed as a Bonus Action. As a Reaction, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and issue a command word, causing the Essence of the Hearth to transform into a flaming cloak. The cloak immediately grants you Temporary Hit Points equal to your Paladin level plus your spellcasting ability modifier. When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage in retaliation. This effect lasts until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted.

errata.problem: The cloak is activated 'As a Reaction' but no trigger is defined. 2024 requires every Reaction to state its trigger: 'A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description.' Without a trigger the feature cannot be legally used.
errata.note: No official Paladin Channel Divinity option uses a Reaction; they use a Bonus Action or the Magic action. This is a genuine departure.
errata.recommendedFix: Define the trigger explicitly. Suggested: 'As a Reaction, which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity...' Alternatively convert to a Bonus Action to match official Channel Divinity options.
errata.appAction: Require the player to record a chosen trigger with DM approval, then enforce it. Default suggestion: 'when you take damage'.

errata.problem: The cloak lasts 'until the Temporary Hit Points are depleted'. In 2024 Temporary Hit Points DO NOT STACK - when you gain new Temporary Hit Points you choose to keep the old pool or take the new one. Taking any other source of Temporary Hit Points (Heroism, Inspiring Leader, Orc Adrenaline Rush, a Chef treat, Aid does not apply) REPLACES the cloak's pool, which by the feature's own wording ends the cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Add: 'The cloak lasts for 1 minute, or until the Temporary Hit Points granted by this feature are reduced to 0, whichever comes first. Gaining Temporary Hit Points from another source does not end this effect.' This decouples the duration from the temp HP pool.
errata.appAction: MANDATORY WARNING. If the cloak is active and the player gains Temporary Hit Points from another source, the app must prompt: 'Accepting these Temporary Hit Points will replace your Hearthfire cloak pool and end the cloak. Continue?'

errata.problem: The retaliation clause has no limit on frequency. 'When you are hit by a melee attack, the creature takes 1d10 Fire damage' triggers on every melee hit, with no once-per-turn or once-per-round cap and no Reaction cost.
errata.comparison: The Fire Shield spell (level 4) deals 2d8 on the same trigger with the same lack of cap, so unlimited retaliation is not unprecedented. However, Fire Shield is a level 4 spell with a hard 10-minute duration; the cloak is a level 3 Channel Divinity whose duration is tied to a temp HP pool that can be large.
errata.assessment: Acceptable as written at low levels. At level 20 with a large temp HP pool this could run for a very long time.
errata.recommendedFix: Optional: cap the duration at 1 minute (see HEARTH-04), which naturally bounds it.
errata.appAction: Implement as written but display the total retaliation damage dealt per encounter so the DM can see the real numbers.

errata.problem: Unclear whether the manifestation must be summoned before the cloak can be used, and whether summoning it costs a separate Bonus Action from the Reaction that activates the cloak. Also undefined: how the manifestation moves, whether it occupies a space, whether it can be attacked or targeted, and whether it provides light while worn as a cloak.
errata.recommendedFix: Rule that the manifestation must be active to transform into the cloak; that it moves with you automatically (treat it as an effect on your person, not a creature or object); that it cannot be attacked or damaged; and that the cloak sheds the same light as the manifestation.
errata.appAction: Record these as a house-ruling block the player fills in once with DM approval.

detail.title: Scorching Ray
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: You create three rays of fire and hurl them at targets within range. You can send them at one target or several. Make a separate ranged spell attack for each ray; each one that hits deals 2d6 Fire damage.

ruleBox.text: Casting this spends your 2nd slot AND your one levelled spell slot for the turn. Nothing else levelled can follow it this turn.

: a Paladin against an airborne target is normally reduced to throwing javelins for 1d6+Strength. Scorching Ray triples that output. If your campaign has dragons, wyverns, or anything with a fly speed, keeping this in mind changes whether those fights are frustrating or fine.

tactics.lead: THE ATTACK-BONUS PROBLEM YOU MUST UNDERSTAND
tactics.body: : each ray is a separate ranged SPELL attack using your Charisma-based spell attack modifier, not your weapon attack. At level 7 with Charisma 16 that is +6. Against a well-armored target you will miss with most rays. Scorching Ray is at its best against LOW-AC targets and at its worst against armored ones — the opposite of your weapon attacks. Read AC before choosing.

— THE REAL DECISION: three rays at one target maximizes the chance of killing it. Three rays at three wounded enemies maximizes the chance of finishing multiple. Focus for bosses, split for clean-up. A ray that overkills a 4-HP goblin is wasted. IT IS AN ACTION, NOT A BONUS ACTION. Casting it means no Attack action that turn, and because of the one-slot-per-turn rule it also means no Divine Smite. Against fire-immune enemies this spell does literally nothing. AT LEVEL 15, ASK YOUR DM ABOUT SMOLDERING SMITE. If it is ruled to cover all your oath's Fire damage rather than only Divine Smite, Scorching Ray becomes resistance-piercing and jumps to the top of your kit. As written it does not apply. See the errata file.

detail.title: Shield of Faith
detail.subtitle: Bonus action · 1st-level slot
detail.whatItDoes: A shimmering field gives one creature within 60 feet a +2 bonus to Armor Class for the duration.

ruleBox.text: Casting this spends your 1st slot AND your one levelled spell slot for the turn. Nothing else levelled can follow it this turn.

tactics.body: Ten minutes of +2 AC for one level 1 slot and a Bonus Action, at 60 feet. That is the best damage-mitigation-per-slot ratio you have.

: at level 7 in Plate (18) with a Shield (+2) and the Defense fighting style (+1) you are at 21. Shield of Faith makes it 23. detail.title: Warding Bond
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Components
facts.value: V, S, M (a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A willing creature you touch gains +1 AC, +1 to all saving throws, and Resistance to all damage. While the bond lasts, every time that creature takes damage, YOU take the same amount of damage. The bond breaks if either of you drops to 0 HP, or if you move more than 60 feet apart.

tactics.body: This is THE Oath of the Hearth spell, mechanically and thematically. 'Guard the hearth' is literally what it does — you take the wound instead of the person you are protecting.

tactics.lead: HOW THE RESISTANCE MATH ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT IS GOOD
tactics.body: : the target takes HALF damage, and YOU take the amount THEY took after resistance. So a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 10 to you. Total damage to the party is unchanged — but you have MOVED it from a d6-hit-die caster with 30 HP onto a d10 Paladin with heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and a healing pool. That is the entire point: you are not reducing damage, you are relocating it onto the character best equipped to absorb it. COMBINE WITH YOUR AURA OF SOLACE (level 7): you have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic. Warding Bond damage is damage YOU take — if your DM rules it retains its damage type (most do), your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN. Warding Bond a caster against a fire-breathing enemy and a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you. That is the strongest defensive combination in the entire Hearth build and your app should surface it explicitly.

tactics.lead: THE COMPONENT COST YOUR APP MUST TRACK
tactics.body: : 100 GP of platinum rings, and they are WORN, not consumed — so you buy them once and reuse them forever. But you must actually own them, a focus cannot substitute, and the target has to be wearing one. Put them in your equipment list now.

tactics.lead: THE 60-FOOT LEASH IS A TACTICAL CONSTRAINT
tactics.body: : the bond breaks if you separate. That means you cannot bond the scout. Bond the person who will stand near you — usually the same person standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection. Your positioning doctrine and your bonding choice should be the same decision.
: it breaks when YOU hit 0. If you are already hurt, bonding someone can kill you both. Check your own HP before casting. Never bond while below half.
: it runs alongside Bless or Compelled Duel. This is a huge deal — it is the only major defensive buff you own that does not compete for Concentration.

: your oath grants Warding Bond as an always-prepared spell at Paladin level 5, and it is ALSO on the standard Paladin spell list. Do not spend one of your seven prepared-spell picks on it. Your app must dedupe this or you will silently waste a prepared slot.

detail.title: Scorching Ray
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: You create three rays of fire and hurl them at targets within range. You can send them at one target or several. Make a separate ranged spell attack for each ray; each one that hits deals 2d6 Fire damage.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

Against a well-armored target you will miss with most rays. Scorching Ray is at its best against LOW-AC targets and at its worst against armored ones — the opposite of your weapon attacks. detail.title: Shield of Faith
detail.subtitle: Bonus action · 1st-level slot
detail.whatItDoes: A shimmering field gives one creature within 60 feet a +2 bonus to Armor Class for the duration.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: Ten minutes of +2 AC for one level 1 slot and a Bonus Action, at 60 feet. That is the best damage-mitigation-per-slot ratio you have.

Against a typical CR 7 attacker with +7 to hit, going from 21 to 23 drops their hit rate from 35%% to 25%% — that is nearly a 30%% cut in incoming damage, sustained for the whole fight.

detail.title: Warding Bond
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Components
facts.value: V, S, M (a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A willing creature you touch gains +1 AC, +1 to all saving throws, and Resistance to all damage. While the bond lasts, every time that creature takes damage, YOU take the same amount of damage. The bond breaks if either of you drops to 0 HP, or if you move more than 60 feet apart.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: This is THE Oath of the Hearth spell, mechanically and thematically. 'Guard the hearth' is literally what it does — you take the wound instead of the person you are protecting.

tactics.lead: HOW THE RESISTANCE MATH ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT IS GOOD
tactics.body: : the target takes HALF damage, and YOU take the amount THEY took after resistance. So a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 10 to you. Total damage to the party is unchanged — but you have MOVED it from a d6-hit-die caster with 30 HP onto a d10 Paladin with heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and a healing pool. That is the entire point: you are not reducing damage, you are relocating it onto the character best equipped to absorb it. COMBINE WITH YOUR AURA OF SOLACE (level 7): you have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic. Warding Bond damage is damage YOU take — if your DM rules it retains its damage type (most do), your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN. Warding Bond a caster against a fire-breathing enemy and a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you. That is the strongest defensive combination in the entire Hearth build and your app should surface it explicitly.

tactics.lead: THE COMPONENT COST YOUR APP MUST TRACK
tactics.body: : 100 GP of platinum rings, and they are WORN, not consumed — so you buy them once and reuse them forever. But you must actually own them, a focus cannot substitute, and the target has to be wearing one. Put them in your equipment list now.

tactics.lead: THE 60-FOOT LEASH IS A TACTICAL CONSTRAINT
tactics.body: : the bond breaks if you separate. That means you cannot bond the scout. Bond the person who will stand near you — usually the same person standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection. Your positioning doctrine and your bonding choice should be the same decision.
: it breaks when YOU hit 0. If you are already hurt, bonding someone can kill you both. Check your own HP before casting. Never bond while below half.
: it runs alongside Bless or Compelled Duel. This is a huge deal — it is the only major defensive buff you own that does not compete for Concentration.

: your oath grants Warding Bond as an always-prepared spell at Paladin level 5, and it is ALSO on the standard Paladin spell list. Do not spend one of your seven prepared-spell picks on it. Your app must dedupe this or you will silently waste a prepared slot.

detail.title: Bless
detail.subtitle: Action · 1st-level slot

facts.label: Components
facts.value: V, S, M (a Holy Symbol worth 5+ GP)

facts.label: Higher Level
facts.value: Target one additional creature for each slot level above 1.

detail.whatItDoes: Up to three creatures you can see add 1d4 to every attack roll and every saving throw they make for the duration. You must hold Concentration to keep it running.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: The single best use of a level 1 slot you have that is not a Smite, and the math says so: 1d4 (avg 2.5) on every attack from four party members over three rounds is worth far more than one 2d8 Divine Smite. Cast it in round one BEFORE you close to melee, because from round two onward your Bonus Action wants to be Divine Smite and your slot budget is one per turn.

: Bless has a 30-foot range at cast time but NO ongoing range limit — once it lands, allies can scatter across the whole battlefield and keep it. So cast it while the party is still stacked at the entry point, then spread out.

: Bless does not stack with itself, but it DOES stack with your Aura of Protection. At level 7 with Charisma 16 that is +1d4 and +3 to every save inside 10 feet of you — a party standing in your aura under Bless is passing saves it would otherwise fail, all fight long. That is the single largest force multiplier a level 7 Paladin can put on the table.

: it is Concentration. Take Resilient (Constitution) or War Caster if you intend to lead with Bless, and stand where you will eat one big hit rather than five small ones — every hit is a separate Concentration save.

detail.title: Burning Hands
detail.subtitle: Action · 1st-level slot

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 3 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A sheet of flame shoots from your outspread fingers in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in the area takes 3d6 Fire damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity save. It also ignites flammable objects in the area that no one is holding or wearing.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: Your only crowd-clearing option until level 17's Flame Strike, and at level 7 it is worth more than it looks.

tactics.lead: THE MATH VERSUS TWO WEAPON ATTACKS
tactics.body: : at level 7 with Extra Attack you swing twice for roughly 20 damage to ONE target. Burning Hands upcast to level 2 is 4d6 (avg 14) to EVERY creature in a 15-foot cone. Against three enemies that is 42 damage for one Action and one level 2 slot. Two or more targets and the spell wins; one target and it loses badly. Count heads before you cast — that is the entire decision.

tactics.lead: THE POSITIONING PROBLEM AND THE FIX
tactics.body: : a 15-foot cone from Self means you must be adjacent to the pack, and a cone from your position will usually catch your own melee allies too — Burning Hands does NOT let you exclude friends. Solve it by being the one who charges the group first, before your party engages. Round one, ride in, detonate the cone, and let your allies mop up from outside the blast. This requires you to be comfortable standing surrounded, which is exactly what your heavy armor, Aura of Protection and Aura of Solace are for. IT SETS FIRE TO THINGS. Read the ignition clause and use it — burn a rope bridge behind you, light an oil slick, set a wooden barricade alight, torch a field between you and pursuers. Terrain damage is a legitimate tactic and this is the only spell you have that does it. FIRE IS THE MOST-RESISTED DAMAGE TYPE IN THE GAME. Against devils, fire elementals, red dragons and most demons, this spell does half or nothing. Always carry a non-Fire answer — Wrathful Smite (Necrotic) and Divine Smite (Radiant) are yours. AT LEVEL 15 SMOLDERING SMITE MAY CHANGE THIS. If your DM rules the subclass's Fire damage to ignore resistance broadly, ask whether it applies here too. As written it does not — see the errata file.

detail.title: Divine Smite
detail.subtitle: Bonus action

facts.label: Casting Time
facts.value: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

facts.label: Damage
facts.value: 2d8 Radiant (+1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Paladin level 2 (Paladin's Smite) - always prepared; one free cast per Long Rest with no slot

detail.whatItDoes: Immediately after you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you spend your Bonus Action to channel 2d8 extra Radiant damage into that hit, plus another 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.

tactics.lead: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN YOUR ENTIRE KIT, AND THE ONE APPS GET WRONG
tactics.body: : 2024 says 'On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.' You cannot cast Bless and then Divine Smite in the same turn. You cannot Smite twice in a turn. One slot, one turn, no exceptions.

tactics.lead: THE LOOPHOLE THAT IS ACTUALLY LEGAL
tactics.body: : your level 2 Paladin's Smite feature lets you cast Divine Smite once per Long Rest WITHOUT EXPENDING A SLOT. The one-slot rule restricts EXPENDING slots. So on one turn per long rest you can legally cast a slotted spell with your Action and free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. Save that turn for the round you need to open hardest.

tactics.lead: SMITE AFTER YOU SEE THE ROLL
tactics.body: : you cast this AFTER the hit is confirmed, not before. Never pre-commit. Attack, see the number, then decide. This is the single biggest reason Divine Smite beats Searing Smite on efficiency — no wasted slots on misses.

tactics.lead: CRITICAL HITS DOUBLE THE SMITE DICE
tactics.body: : on a crit you roll all the attack's damage dice twice, and the Smite dice are part of that attack's damage. A crit with a level 2 slot is 6d8 of Smite. So SMITE ON CRITS, ALWAYS, without hesitation, even against a target you would not otherwise spend a slot on.

: with Extra Attack you get two swings. Take the first swing. If it crits, Smite immediately. If it hits normally, hold — take the second swing, and if THAT crits, Smite it instead. You only get one Smite per turn either way, so let the dice tell you which hit deserves it.

: Fiends and Undead take +1d8. Concentrating enemy casters are the real prize — a big Smite forces a Concentration save at DC 10 or half the damage, and a 2nd-level Smite averaging 13 means a DC 10 save, while a crit for 27 means a DC 13. Dropping an enemy's Wall of Force or Hold Person is worth more than the raw damage.
: the casting time explicitly names Unarmed Strikes. If you are grappling something and cannot draw a weapon, you can still Smite it.

: no bows, no crossbows. Thrown melee weapons (javelin, handaxe) are a genuine RAW dispute — make this a configurable toggle in your app and ask your DM which way it rules. HEARTH SYNERGY (level 15): Smoldering Smite adds 1d8 Fire that ignores resistance AND immunity. Note your subclass text says 'Magic action to cast Divine Smite' — that is a homebrew error, Divine Smite is a Bonus Action spell in 2024 and never a Magic action. See the errata file.

detail.title: Faerie Fire
detail.subtitle: Action · 1st-level slot

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 3 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: Each creature in a 20-foot Cube within range is outlined in light of a color you choose unless it succeeds on a Dexterity save. Affected creatures shed Dim Light in a 10-foot radius, cannot benefit from the Invisible condition, and attack rolls against them have Advantage.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: The best action-economy spell your oath gives you at level 3, and the one most Paladins underuse. ADVANTAGE FOR THE WHOLE PARTY ON A 20-FOOT CUBE. Not one target — a cube. Catch three enemies and every attack your party makes against any of them has Advantage for a minute. Advantage is worth roughly +5 to hit. Across a four-person party over three rounds that is a larger damage swing than any Smite you can cast at this level, by a wide margin.

— this is why it lands. Most heavy brutes, undead, oozes and constructs have poor Dexterity. It is the opposite of your Smite spells' save profile, which makes it the right opener against exactly the enemies your Smites struggle to debuff. IT IS A HARD COUNTER TO INVISIBILITY AND HIDING. 2024 folded hiding into the Invisible condition, and Faerie Fire explicitly stops a creature from benefiting from Invisible. Rogues, drow in Darkness, invisible stalkers, anything that keeps vanishing — Faerie Fire ends the problem for a minute. It also works on a target you cannot see, because it targets an AREA. Blanket the square you think the assassin is standing in.

tactics.lead: THE OPENING ROUND DOCTRINE FOR A HEARTH PALADIN
tactics.body: : round one, cast Faerie Fire from 60 feet as you close. It costs your Action but not your Bonus Action, so you can still summon your Hearthfire Manifest. From round two you are in melee with the whole party swinging at Advantage. That is a better round one than walking up and hitting something once.

IT DOES NOT COUNT AGAINST YOUR PREPARED SPELLS. Free, always ready, and it is not on the normal Paladin list, so your oath is genuinely giving you something you could never otherwise have.

detail.title: Warding Bond
detail.subtitle: Action · 2nd-level slot

facts.label: Components
facts.value: V, S, M (a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear)

facts.label: Granted by
facts.value: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared

detail.whatItDoes: A willing creature you touch gains +1 AC, +1 to all saving throws, and Resistance to all damage. While the bond lasts, every time that creature takes damage, YOU take the same amount of damage. The bond breaks if either of you drops to 0 HP, or if you move more than 60 feet apart.

ruleBox.text: You have already spent a levelled spell slot this turn. Under the 2024 rules that is one per turn, so this cannot be cast until your next turn.

tactics.body: This is THE Oath of the Hearth spell, mechanically and thematically. 'Guard the hearth' is literally what it does — you take the wound instead of the person you are protecting.

tactics.lead: HOW THE RESISTANCE MATH ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT IS GOOD
tactics.body: : the target takes HALF damage, and YOU take the amount THEY took after resistance. So a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 10 to you. Total damage to the party is unchanged — but you have MOVED it from a d6-hit-die caster with 30 HP onto a d10 Paladin with heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and a healing pool. That is the entire point: you are not reducing damage, you are relocating it onto the character best equipped to absorb it. COMBINE WITH YOUR AURA OF SOLACE (level 7): you have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic. Warding Bond damage is damage YOU take — if your DM rules it retains its damage type (most do), your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN. Warding Bond a caster against a fire-breathing enemy and a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you. That is the strongest defensive combination in the entire Hearth build and your app should surface it explicitly.

tactics.lead: THE COMPONENT COST YOUR APP MUST TRACK
tactics.body: : 100 GP of platinum rings, and they are WORN, not consumed — so you buy them once and reuse them forever. But you must actually own them, a focus cannot substitute, and the target has to be wearing one. Put them in your equipment list now.

tactics.lead: THE 60-FOOT LEASH IS A TACTICAL CONSTRAINT
tactics.body: : the bond breaks if you separate. That means you cannot bond the scout. Bond the person who will stand near you — usually the same person standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection. Your positioning doctrine and your bonding choice should be the same decision.
: it breaks when YOU hit 0. If you are already hurt, bonding someone can kill you both. Check your own HP before casting. Never bond while below half.
: it runs alongside Bless or Compelled Duel. This is a huge deal — it is the only major defensive buff you own that does not compete for Concentration.

: your oath grants Warding Bond as an always-prepared spell at Paladin level 5, and it is ALSO on the standard Paladin spell list. Do not spend one of your seven prepared-spell picks on it. Your app must dedupe this or you will silently waste a prepared slot.
